claims.text: Plasma nitriding Ti-6Al-4V at approximately 700°C for 10 hours in an ammonia/hydrogen atmosphere will produce a controlled nitride surface layer.
Fine-tuning the nitriding parameters and using controlled inert-gas cooling will limit nitride-layer thickness and prevent brittleness.
The treatment will form a thin, hardened TiN compound layer at the surface.
The TiN compound layer will be underlain by a nitrogen-doped alpha-Ti diffusion zone.
The diffusion zone will provide a smooth transition in mechanical properties between the surface layer and substrate.
During plasma nitriding, nitrogen diffuses into the Ti-6Al-4V surface and forms TiN.
The graded diffusion zone reduces interfacial stress concentration.
Reduced interfacial stress concentration provides improved load support.
The nitrided graded layer improves resistance to abrasive and adhesive wear.
Plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V will have approximately two to three times the surface microhardness of untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V will exhibit a significant decrease in wear volume relative to untreated samples under identical sliding conditions.
The predicted hardness and wear benefits are expected under ambient-temperature sliding against a hardened counter-body.
Whether the treatment remains effective at extreme temperatures or under highly cyclic mechanical loads is unresolved.
Over-nitriding can cause brittleness and spallation of the nitride layer.
